name: Convex Finance
rootCause: ConvexFinance officially tweeted that a DNS attack caused users to approve malicious contracts on some interactions on the website, and the problem has been fixed.

descriptions.text: ConvexFinance officially tweeted that a DNS attack caused users to approve malicious contracts on some interactions on the website, and the problem has been fixed.

Convex Finance's domain was hijacked on June 23,24, 2022, redirecting users to a phishing site that prompted approvals for malicious smart contracts. Only three wallets suffered losses, totaling about $14,000 in tokens. The core protocol contracts remained secure, and Convex pledged full reimbursement for victims. A compromised NameCheap customer support agent allowed the attacker to change DNS records and redirect convexfinance.com to a malicious front end. This spoofed the real site and tricked users into approving contracts nearly identical to Convex's official addresses.
